description:
The food.gdt dataset is open in Gretl. It contains household survey data with 'food_exp' (weekly food expenditure) and 'income' (weekly income).

Perform an inequality analysis:
1. Calculate the Gini coefficient for the 'income' variable.
2. Calculate the Gini coefficient for the 'food_exp' variable.
3. Create a text file at /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/inequality_report.txt and write these two values into it (label them clearly).
4. Generate a Lorenz curve graph for the 'income' variable (View > Graph specified vars > Lorenz curve). Save this graph as a PNG image to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/lorenz_income.png.

Note: You can find Gini coefficients in the 'Summary statistics' view or by using the 'gini' command in the console.
